pricing.freeTierCaps: 30 credits per day, resetting every 24 hours; up to 3 uploads per day and 2 images per prompt; free outputs are public and lack commercial-use rights.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (up to -20%); paid subscription credits reset monthly
pricing.hiddenCosts: Unused subscription credits do not roll over; paid users can buy non-expiring top-ups only in 200/400/800/1,600-credit packs, but pack prices are not publicly listed; Teams requires at least 2 seats.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Recraft, organize prompts and local vector or raster generation jobs for branded assets. The hard boundary is proprietary design model, vector generation quality, style controls, and compute, plus frontier models, compute, and data.
coreLoopDIY: Organize prompts and local vector or raster generation jobs for branded assets, submit them to a user-owned model server, and keep outputs reproducible.
requirements: GPU-capable machine or user-supplied generation API
whatYouLose: proprietary design model, vector generation quality, style controls, and compute
replacementScope: local workflow manager, not a model replacement
ongoingBurden: GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Recraft because the product value is the model and compute fleet, not the prompt box around it. The recurring cost buys GPU procurement, model licensing, safety filters, queueing, storage, and rapid model replacement, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: ComfyUI
priorArt.desc: Node-based open-source diffusion workflow engine with a large ecosystem.

rejectedAlternatives.name: ComfyUI
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Raster generation is thoroughly covered; brand-aware vector generation and editable SVG output are not.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a local workflow manager, not a model replacement DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Recraft in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ComfyUI as a local worker, and a small React frontend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize prompts and local vector or raster generation jobs for branded assets, submit them to a user-owned model server, and keep outputs reproducible.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create prompt, negative-prompt, seed, dimensions, model, and workflow controls.
Submit jobs only to the local ComfyUI endpoint configured in .env.
Record exact generation parameters and workflow JSON beside every output.
Build a searchable contact sheet with compare, favorite, annotate, and rerun actions.
Support local image-to-image and mask inputs without uploading them elsewhere.
Show estimated VRAM needs and fail clearly when a workflow or model is missing.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out training a new frontier model.
Deliberately leave out copying a vendor's proprietary model or dataset.
Deliberately leave out public generation hosting and moderation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
